nodes.title: Model the request as one status union
nodes.why: A discriminated union makes impossible combinations such as loading and error at the same time unrepresentable, and TypeScript narrows `request.members` or `request.message` inside each branch.
nodes.alternative: Keep `isLoading`, `error` and `members` as three separate state values.
nodes.tradeoff: The union needs a type up front, but every render branch and every test then reads from a single source of truth.

nodes.title: Reset to loading at the start of every request
nodes.why: Switching the data source must show the loading line immediately; without this reset the rows from the previous source stay visible while the new request is in flight.
nodes.alternative: Keep the previous rows and show a small spinner next to them.
nodes.tradeoff: A full reset flashes the list on every switch, but it never shows data that belongs to another source.

nodes.title: Ignore stale responses with a cleanup flag
nodes.why: When the mode changes before the previous request resolves, the cleanup flips `cancelled` so the old `.then` and `.catch` return without touching state.
nodes.alternative: Pass an `AbortController` signal into the fetch and abort it in the cleanup.
nodes.tradeoff: The flag cannot stop the network call, but the fake API takes no signal and the flag still prevents the stale update.

nodes.title: Map an empty list to its own state
nodes.why: An empty response is a successful request with nothing to show; giving it a dedicated status keeps the empty copy out of the success branch.
nodes.alternative: Store the empty array as success and check `members.length` in the JSX.
nodes.tradeoff: One more status to render, but the component never mixes list rendering with empty-state copy.

nodes.title: Normalise unknown errors before rendering
nodes.why: A rejection is typed `unknown`; the `instanceof Error` check turns it into a readable string and avoids rendering `undefined`.
nodes.tradeoff: The helper is a few extra lines, but it keeps the error branch typed and readable.

nodes.title: Run the request from the mode and the retry counter
nodes.why: Both a source change and a retry should run the same request path; listing both in the dependency array keeps one fetch implementation.
nodes.alternative: Call `fetchTeam` from the select handler and again from the Retry handler.
nodes.tradeoff: Handlers that fetch duplicate the state transitions and are easy to drift; the effect centralises them.

nodes.title: Retry by bumping a counter
nodes.why: Incrementing `attempt` changes a dependency, so the effect re-runs with the current mode and the loading reset, cleanup and mapping all apply again.
nodes.alternative: Toggle a boolean or set the request back to loading from the click handler.
nodes.tradeoff: A counter always changes, while a boolean toggled twice can skip a re-run.

nodes.title: Show Retry only in the error branch
nodes.why: The button is part of the error state; rendering it from `request.status` keeps it out of the loading, empty and success branches without extra flags.
nodes.alternative: Always render the button and disable it outside the error state.
nodes.tradeoff: A conditional button changes the layout on error, but the tests and the user only see it when it can do something.

nodes.title: Key rows by the member id
nodes.why: Stable keys let React reconcile the list correctly when a retry replaces the members array.
nodes.alternative: Use the array index as the key.
nodes.tradeoff: Index keys work for a static list but break ordering and focus when items move.
